items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: you know before that the band was playing like Richard Evans’ “MacArthur Park” and all that.

ctx.x: When you took over the group, and by the way I have to give Mr. Herman a lot of credit for being open-minded about adding new material.

That’s the greatest part of that actually, the reason why I stayed there for all of those years is because everybody came in — you take Tony Klatka, Alan Broadbent, Bill Stapleton, they all come in — they wrote what they wanted to and he would just approve it every time. And I mean Alan Vizutti, you know, the trumpet player, he’d come in with the “Fire Dance” and my tunes too. But he wasn’t there when my tunes — actually I think so, no, I don’t think he ever heard my tunes. But no, I mean you know Fedchock did a…

was planned. All the sessions were planned. But one day before, Woody comes up to me and says, “You know, Frank, we need a hot number.” I says, “Have I got a hot number for you.” And so we performed it. I wonder if you ever heard of the tune, I don’t know if you have.
